recipes.name: Asian Chicken (Asian marinade)
ingredients: 1 - 1.5 lb / 500 - 750g chicken thigh fillets (, skinless boneless or small chicken breasts (see notes))
3 cloves garlic (, minced (garlic press or finely grated))
2 tbsp light soy sauce (or all-purpose soy sauce (see notes))
1 1/2 tbsp Chinese cooking wine OR Mirin ((see notes))
instructions: Breast - If using chicken breast, cover with plastic wrap or baking paper and lightly pound the thicker end using the flat end of a meat mallet, a rolling pin (or even your fist!) to the pound fat end of chicken breast to about 1.7 cm / 2/3″ even thickness (not required for thigh). If you have very big chicken breasts, split in half horizontally instead to make thinner steaks.
Marinade - Mix Marinade ingredients together. Add chicken and mix to coat. Marinade in the fridge for a minimum of 1 hour or up to overnight. (For breast, I recommend overnight).,

Cook - Heat oil in a large non stick skillet or BBQ over medium high heat. (See notes for other cooking methods) Add chicken and cook until each side is dark golden brown and chicken is cooked through (about 3 minutes each side for thighs, 2 minutes for breast). Transfer to plate, cover loosely with foil and rest for 3 minutes. (If using a pan, cook in batches - don't crowd the pan)
Rest and serve - Garnish with chillies, shallots and sesame seeds if desired. Serve with white rice and slices of cucumber.

page_recipe_notes: Recipe Notes: 1. Substitutions: Chicken – tenderloin will also work, cook for 2 minutes on each side. For breast, it’s best to pound to even thickness so it will cook through evenly (more important for breast than thigh as it’s leaner so overcooked parts = drier) Garlic / ginger – 1 tsp garlic / ginger powder (but please try to use fresh, it’s much better. Asian cooking doesn’t use garlic / ginger powder) Soy sauce – Use tamari for gluten-free. Do not use dark soy sauce (too intense). Fish sauce could also be used, but reduce to 1 1/2 tbsp (because fish sauce is saltier) Tomato ketchup – Australian tomato sauce can be used. Oyster sauce – hoisin sauce (but note it has a mild Chinese 5 Spice Powder flavour which is nice), or vegetarian oyster sauce for shell-fish free Chinese cooking wine (aka Shaoxing Cooking Wine) – Asian rice wine used commonly in Asian cooking. Mirin is an excellent alternative. This is the secret ingredient in the marinade! Sub with dry sherry (best option), sake (next best) or marsala. To make it non alcoholic, use 2 tbsp chicken stock/broth PLUS 1 tbsp extra oyster sauce. Sriracha – swap out with any other chili paste or finely chopped fresh chili or powder. Add a tiny bit (1 tsp or so) of vinegar (white, malt, apple cider), lime or lemon juice (because Sriracha is the “sour” component in this marinade) Brown sugar – white sugar, honey or maple syrup Sesame oil – this can be left out. 2. Cooking alternative – This can also be baked in a 180C/350F oven for around 20 minutes or grilled / broiled on high. It’s also great made as skewers. 3. To make ahead: Place chicken and marinade in a ziplock bag and place in the freezer straight away. Defrost before cooking. The chicken marinades as it freezes / defrosts. Cook per directions. Cooked chicken doesn’t freeze that well – the chicken itself is fine but the marinade flavour fades.
